applied.problem: Too general: the joined box shows the drawn state, not now; a lever at one end brings in either outer box; the left box's arrows and A on the piston side are one layout; the quote's other-phases qualifier was dropped; a check valve is drawn as a ball

The rule of thumb fails for a lever valve drawn with one lever at one end, which brings in either outer box; 'nothing operating the valve' is absolute though a valve held by a cam is drawn operated; the worked example uses the left box's arrows and A on the piston side without stating them.

'Oil goes one way, from the pump to the tank' while current goes round a loop is wrong: oil also goes round a loop through the tank; the real difference is that mains current reverses while oil flows one way round.
Screen 10's why says a plain check valve holds a load, but a plain check valve in the line would also stop the load ever being lowered; load holding uses a check valve that a pilot line opens.
